original_title: Netflix India Expanding Into Under-90-minute Films, Multiple Projects in the Works
summary_en: Netflix India is reportedly developing a slate of films designed to be watched in under 90 minutes. This move signals a significant shift in content strategy, aiming to capture audiences with shorter attention spans.

en.title: Netflix India Bets Big on Under-90-Minute Films for 2026
en.summary: Netflix India is reportedly developing a slate of films designed to be watched in under 90 minutes. This move signals a significant shift in content strategy, aiming to capture audiences with shorter attention spans.
en.body:
## A New Pace for Indian Cinema

Netflix India is gearing up for a significant content expansion in 2026, with a notable focus on producing films under the 90-minute mark. This initiative, driven by a desire to cater to viewers seeking more concise entertainment options, aims to broaden the platform's creative horizons and tap into a growing demand for shorter, yet complete, cinematic experiences. While Netflix remains committed to ambitious, full-length features, this new ecosystem allows for experimentation with a wider array of creators, subjects, and storytelling techniques that might not fit the traditional runtime. The strategy aligns perfectly with how many consumers, particularly those on mobile, engage with content – fitting a full movie experience into smaller pockets of free time between daily activities.

This move isn't just about viewer convenience; it also presents compelling creative and economic advantages. Certain genres, such as taut thrillers, intimate dramas, and high-concept comedies, often benefit from a tighter narrative structure. By embracing shorter runtimes, Netflix India can collaborate with emerging talent and explore niche subjects that might be challenging to sustain for two or three hours. This approach allows for more focused storytelling, ensuring that every minute counts and delivering a satisfying, impactful experience without demanding a significant time commitment from the audience.

## What This Means for Fans

For dedicated fans of Indian cinema and global Netflix subscribers alike, this development is an exciting prospect. It signals a commitment from Netflix to diversify its offerings and cater to evolving viewing habits. The prospect of finishing a compelling story during a lunch break or before settling in for the evening is incredibly appealing. Furthermore, the emphasis on empowering new creators and exploring diverse subjects suggests a richer, more varied content pipeline. Upcoming projects like **Chor Nikal Ke Bhaga 2** and **Ginny Weds Sunny 2**, reportedly part of this strategy, hint at the kind of engaging, compact narratives viewers can expect. This move could lead to a resurgence of tightly plotted genre films and a platform for stories that might otherwise struggle to find funding or distribution in a traditional film industry.

## What's Next

With 2026 on the horizon, Netflix India's content slate is expected to be packed with these innovative, shorter films. While specific release dates for many projects are yet to be announced, the strategic direction is clear: more compact, compelling stories designed for the modern viewer. Fans should keep an eye on official Netflix India announcements for further details on these exciting new productions.

content_raw: Picture Credit: Alamy Have you ever wished for movies that can be finished during a lunch break or a gap between work and dinner? Well, Netflix India seems to be exploring that very proposition with under-90-minute feature films designed for quick viewing.  According to multiple sources, the Indian content arm of the American streaming platform is increasingly embracing compact 60-to-85-minute-long films for audiences who may not always have time to commit to conventional 2- to 3-hour movies. Broadening the Creative Canvas Netflix hasn’t publicly defined this as a separate production category or financing model. People familiar with the development describe it instead as a part of Netflix’s broader strategy of expansion and growth. The company remains committed to investing in ambitious full-length feature films across genres and languages, with the new “under 90-minute” movie ecosystem further expanding the creative canvas by experimenting with new creators, subjects, and storytelling spaces. As Indian feature films continue to resonate across the globe, the streamer is doubling down on its film strategy. The latest endeavor allows Netflix to collaborate with more young creative voices and explore genres and subjects that might not otherwise be possible to make as a conventional three-hour film. The strategy aligns with the streamer’s consumption model because a 90-minute film can work even when somebody has only a small window between activities. This provides a complete movie experience to viewers without asking them to commit two-and-a-half hours. There are creative and economic considerations as well. Some genres, such as taut thrillers, intimate family dramas and high-concept comedies, often work better at a tighter runtime. Furthermore, production is cheaper, turnaround is faster, and it allows the platform to experiment with unconventional content. Early Success with Greater Kalesh Picture Credit: Netflix Netflix India has been attempting to experiment with under-90-minute featurettes since last year.
